docs.title: Prep
docs.text:
1. Cauliflower (2lb), core and cut into florets (6c)
  2. Mince garlic (1) into a bowl, pour lemon juice (1) over it, let sit while the cauliflower roasts - this tames the garlic
  3. Mince parsley
  4. Set aside
    • tahini (.25c)
    • warm water (.5c)
    • mixed olives (.33c)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Oven to 400
  2. Toss cauliflower with olive oil (2tbsp) and salt (.75tsp)
  3. Roast, stirring once, until tender and browned (35m)
  4. Food processor
    1. Roasted cauliflower
    2. Olive oil (2tbsp)
    3. Garlic and lemon juice
    4. Tahini (.25c)
    5. Warm water (.5c)
    6. Salt (.75tsp)
    7. Blend until completely smooth, more water if needed
  5. Spoon onto a plate, make a well in the middle, drizzle with olive oil (1tbsp)
  6. Garnish with olives (.33c) and parsley, serve with crackers

docs.title: Prep
docs.text:
1. Crusts out of the box to room temperature (15m)
  2. Thaw mixed vegetables (2c)
  3. Chop onion (.33c)
  4. Shred cooked chicken (2.5c)
  5. Line 9in pie plate with one crust, pressed to the side and bottom
  6. Set aside
    • chicken broth (1.75c)
    • milk (.5c)
    • flour (.33c)
    • salt (.5tsp)
    • pepper (.25tsp)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Oven to 425
  2. Saucepan, medium heat, butter (.33c)
    1. Add onion (.33c), cook until tender (2m)
    2. Stir in flour (.33c), salt (.5tsp), pepper (.25tsp) until blended
    3. Gradually stir in broth (1.75c) and milk (.5c), until bubbly and thick
    4. Stir in chicken (2.5c) and vegetables (2c), off heat
  3. Spoon filling into the lined pie plate
  4. Top with the second crust, fold the edge under, seal and flute
  5. Cut slits in the top crust
  6. Bake (15m)
  7. Cover the crust edge with foil, bake until golden (15-25m)
  8. Rest (5m)

docs.title: Shopping
docs.text:
• Produce
    • ginger (2in, .33c)
    • broccoli florets (1lb)
    • scallions or cilantro
  • Dairy (none)
  • Middle
    • chicken breasts, boneless skinless (1.5lb)
    • coconut milk, unsweetened (.5c)
    • gochujang paste (2tbsp)
  • Staples
    • canola oil (2tbsp)
    • turbinado sugar (3tbsp) or light brown sugar (2tbsp)
    • soy sauce, low-sodium (2tbsp)
    • kosher salt
    • black pepper
    • white rice

docs.title: Prep
docs.text:
1. Cut chicken (1.5lb) into 1.5in pieces, season with salt and pepper
  2. Ginger (2in), peel and cut into matchsticks (.33c)
  3. Broccoli (1lb), cut florets into 2in pieces
  4. Slice scallions or chop cilantro for serving
  5. Sauce bowl
    • coconut milk (.5c)
    • turbinado sugar (3tbsp)
    • gochujang paste (2tbsp)
    • soy sauce (2tbsp)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Start the rice
  2. Large nonstick skillet, med-high heat, canola oil (2tbsp)
    1. Add chicken, stir occasionally until golden all over (3m)
    2. Add ginger (.33c), stir until softened (2m)
    3. Add the sauce bowl, bring to a simmer, stirring until the gochujang dissolves
    4. Reduce to med-low, simmer until chicken is cooked through (5m)
  3. Meanwhile, blanch broccoli (1lb) in salted boiling water until crisp-tender (2m), then drain
  4. Plate chicken and broccoli, spoon the sauce over, serve with rice and the scallions or cilantro

docs.title: Prep
docs.text:
1. Drain and rinse chickpeas (15oz)
  2. Quarter tomatoes (1 pint)
  3. Slice zucchini (1) and yellow squash (1) into very thin rounds
  4. Chop shallot (.5c) fine, press garlic (2)
  5. Slice olives (.33c) thin, crumble feta (1c)
  6. Chop basil or parsley (.33c)
  7. Dressing, in a large serving bowl, whisk
    • olive oil (.33c)
    • lemon juice (2tbsp, up to 4 to taste)
    • shallot (.5c)

    • fine sea salt (.5tsp)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Cook couscous (1.33c) al dente per the package, drain off excess water
  2. Large skillet, med-low heat, toast pine nuts (.33c) until lightly golden and fragrant - they burn fast - then into a bowl to cool
  3. Add couscous to the dressing bowl, toss to coat
  4. Top with and stir through
    • pine nuts (.33c)
    • chickpeas (15oz)
    • tomatoes (1 pint)
    • feta (1c)
    • olives (.33c)
    • zucchini and yellow squash
    • basil or parsley (.33c)
  5. Salt, pepper and more lemon juice to taste
  6. Best after chilling (30m)

1. Slice shallot (1) thin
  2. Drain and rinse chickpeas (14oz)
  3. Chop chives (.25c) and mint (3-4tbsp, opt)
  4. Kale (4-5 stalks), destem and tear into bite-size pieces
  5. Kale dressing bowl, whisk
    • olive oil (3tbsp)
    • red wine vinegar (1tbsp)
    • maple syrup (1tbsp)

  6. Set aside
    • diced tomatoes (14oz)
    • vegetable broth (.75c)
    • pearl couscous (.5c)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Skillet, medium heat, olive oil (2tbsp)
    1. Add shallot (1) and cumin (.5tsp), saute until softened (5m)
    2. Add chickpeas (14oz), mash gently a few times for texture
    3. Add tomatoes (14oz), bring to a simmer
    4. Add broth (.75c), salt (1tsp), couscous (.5c), simmer
    5. Cover, low heat, until couscous is soft and has absorbed most of the liquid (6-8m)
    6. Stir in chives (.25c)
  2. Massage kale with its dressing until tender (1-2m)
  3. Serve the couscous with the kale alongside, topped with mint (opt) and feta (opt)

docs.title: Prep
docs.text:
1. Rinse masoor dal (1c) in a fine-mesh sieve
  2. Chop onion (1) coarsely, garlic (2) fine
  3. Grate ginger (1tsp)
  4. Chop spinach (3c) coarsely
  5. Halve the lime (1)
  6. Seed bowl
    • black mustard seeds (.5tsp)
    • cumin seeds (.5tsp)
    • fennel seed (.5tsp)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Start the rice
  2. Saucepan: dal (1c) and water (3c), boil over med-high heat
    1. Skim the foam until it stops foaming (3m)
    2. Stir in turmeric (.25tsp)
    3. Reduce to med-low, partially cover, simmer until tender (25-30m)
    4. Off heat, squeeze in juice from half the lime, stir in salt (1tsp)
  3. High-sided skillet, med-high heat, ghee (2tbsp)
    1. Add the seed bowl, cook until mustard seeds pop (seconds)
    2. Reduce to medium, add chile (1), stir to coat
    3. Add onion (1), stir until translucent and softened (5m)
    4. Add garlic (2) and ginger (1tsp), until fragrant (30s)
    5. Add spinach (3c) and salt (.5tsp), until wilted but still bright green (1m)
    6. Off heat, squeeze in juice from the remaining lime half
  4. Stir the spinach mixture into the dal, salt to taste
  5. Serve over rice, topped with cilantro and lime wedges

docs.title: Prep
docs.text:
1. Drain tofu (14-16oz), cut into cubes
  2. Zest oranges (1-2tsp) and juice them (6tbsp)
  3. Marinade bowl, whisk
    • soy sauce (1tbsp)
    • toasted sesame oil (1tbsp)
    • fine salt (.5tsp)
    • white or black pepper (pinch)
  4. Add tofu, stir to coat
  5. Add cornstarch (1-2tbsp), stir to coat
  6. Sauce bowl
    • orange zest (1-2tsp)
    • orange juice (6tbsp)
    • honey (.25c)
    • cider vinegar (1tsp)
    • ground ginger (.25tsp)
    • crushed red pepper flakes (.25tsp)

docs.title: Cook
docs.text:
1. Air fryer to 400
  2. Tofu to the basket, air fry until crisp (11-13m), shaking halfway
  3. Meanwhile reduce the sauce in the microwave
    1. Microwave (2m), whisk
    2. Microwave (1m), whisk
    3. Repeat until it looks like melted honey and has reduced to just under .5c
  4. Drizzle half the sauce over the tofu, stir to coat

docs.text:
1. Line 8x8 pan with foil, spray with cooking spray
  2. Chop graham crackers (5, 2c) - keep the crumbs
  3. Microwave-safe bowl: melt butter (.5c) on high (1m), let cool a moment so the egg does not scramble
  4. Whisk in until smooth
    • egg (1)
    • light brown sugar (1c)
    • vanilla extract (1tbsp)
  5. Stir in flour (.75c) just until combined - do not overmix
  6. Fold in

    • semi-sweet chocolate chips (1c)
